solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Agent bound to be reinstated

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
laced means tied up or bound, as a shoe is

explanation.surface: A secret agent, fettered, is determined to be restored to his old post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to be' reads as 'certain to be', but 'bound' gives LACED and 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something replaced has been put back in its former position, which is what reinstated means.

clue.text: Motor that could be on fire

definitions.meaning: a motor is a machine that drives something, like the power unit of a car
a fire appliance, the red truck that fire crews ride on, is a fire ___

explanation.definitionFit: An engine is a motor, and a fire engine is the vehicle that rushes to a blaze.

clue.text: Fifty, in turn, give tongue

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Fifty people, each in turn, are told to speak up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and lingo is a casual word for a language or jargon.

clue.text: Pretend to be ill, we hear, to get a drink

indicators.note: we hear says the letters that follow come from words spoken out loud

parts.note: to fake being unwell is to put on a sham pain

explanation.surface: Someone fakes sickness to be given a restorative tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAM PAIN, said out loud, comes out close to the name of the sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a sparkling wine, a celebratory drink from the French region of that name.

clue.text: Course set south in barren terrain

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for south goes inside the word for barren land

parts.note: a desert is a barren area of land

explanation.surface: A route is plotted heading south across a wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a route, matching the surface, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert is the sweet course served at the end of a meal.

clue.text: To step back will give foot protection

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back says the word for a step is to be read in the other direction

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: Stepping backwards, you would be wise to protect your feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'step back' reads as retreating, but 'back' only turns the word for a step around.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is the reinforced front of a boot that protects the toes.

clue.text: Adjusted number on front of door

parts.note: a number is a song or piece of music, a tune

indicators.note: front of picks out the opening letter of the next word, door

explanation.surface: A house number on a front door has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a figure on a door, but it is a musical number; in a down clue 'on' puts it above D.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that has been tuned has been adjusted to the right pitch.

clue.text: Property conveyance?

parts.note: reads like the legal transfer of property, but is a vehicle (a conveyance) called after a landed property

explanation.walkthrough: Conveyancing is the legal work of transferring property, which the surface suggests; the answer is a roomy car with a load space at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a car with a long rear load area, which British English names after a country estate.

clue.text: Was aggressive at first, then changed course

indicators.note: then says the following piece comes after the first

parts.note: taken as written
a sailing boat that tacks changes course by turning into the wind

explanation.surface: Someone who started out hostile later took a different line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first, then' simply orders the pieces: AT comes first, then TACKED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have attacked is to have been aggressive, assaulting someone.

clue.text: Business fixed in minutes

parts.note: the items of business a meeting settles beforehand and which are recorded in its minutes

explanation.walkthrough: 'minutes' suggests a short time, but it means the written record of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of business to be dealt with at a meeting, set down in advance.

clue.text: Holiness surprisingly intact in the outskirts of Surrey

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters between the outer letters of Surrey
outskirts are the edges, so take only the first and last letters of Surrey
surprisingly suggests the letters of intact turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A sacred site remains unspoiled on the edge of an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intact' looks like a description of the holiness, but 'surprisingly' marks it for rearranging. Surrey is a county just south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is the quality of being holy or sacred, a synonym of holiness.

clue.text: Stumbling upon clue for 'disconnect'

indicators.note: stumbling suggests the letters trip over and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A solver chances on the clue that means 'disconnect'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumbling upon' reads as 'finding by chance', but 'Stumbling' rearranges UPON and CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple railway carriages is to disconnect them from each other.

clue.text: Part the cad needed to play

indicators.note: something needed to play is set in motion, so these letters are moved about

explanation.surface: The bounder was required to take a role in the production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like an acting role, matching 'play', but it is a verb meaning separate.
explanation.definitionFit: To part two things is to separate them, which is to detach one from the other.

clue.text: There's a poor beginning but a capital ending to this tale

definitions.text: There's a poor beginning but a capital ending to this tale

parts.words: There's a poor beginning but a capital ending to this tale
parts.note: a story that starts in poverty and finishes with a fortune, capital meaning money

explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a word for excellent, but here it means wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rags-to-riches story tells of someone who rises from poverty to great wealth.

clue.text: Foreign city bank headed by scoundrel

indicators.note: headed by says the word for scoundrel sits on top of the word for bank in this down clue

parts.note: a rotter is an old British word for a scoundrel
a dam is an embankment that holds back water

explanation.surface: Abroad, a crooked villain takes control of a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests a financial institution, but it is a bank holding back water.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major port city in the Netherlands, foreign from a British setter's view.

clue.text: Communist and German worker laid off

parts.note: Red is a common term for a communist
und is the German word for and
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist and a German labourer have lost their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German worker' looks like one phrase, but 'and German' gives UND and 'worker' alone gives ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker made redundant has been laid off because the job no longer exists.

clue.text: Important person that's going round in London

definitions.meaning: a big shot or person of influence
a giant observation wheel, like the London Eye on the Thames, which turns slowly

explanation.definitionFit: A big wheel is slang for a person of importance, and also a large fairground Ferris wheel.

clue.text: Infant prodigy is hardly to be marvelled at

definitions.meaning: a child of remarkable talent, a small marvel
the phrase means it is not surprising

explanation.definitionFit: A small child genius is a little wonder, and 'little wonder' also means no surprise.

clue.text: Craft operatives who twist one's arm

indicators.note: twist suggests wrenching the letters into a different shape

explanation.surface: Boat workers who are bullies, forcing people to comply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist one's arm' is the idiom for pressuring someone, but 'twist' rearranges the letters of ONE'S ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarsmen are rowers, the people who work a craft such as a rowing boat.

clue.text: They are unqualified to deal with complaints of bird sounds

definitions.text: They are unqualified to deal with complaints
definitions.meaning: fake doctors who treat illnesses, complaints meaning ailments

explanation.definitionFit: Quacks are charlatan doctors, and quacks are also the noises ducks make.

clue.text: Ways to get round little children's demands

indicators.note: to get round says the word for ways goes around the word for little

parts.note: STS is the abbreviation for streets, which are ways
wee is a Scottish word for little

explanation.surface: Tricks for coaxing little ones into getting what they want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get round' reads as 'persuade', which fits the coaxing surface, but here it is a container signal; 'children's demands' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweets are sugary treats, which small children constantly ask for.

clue.text: Loves an anagram to work out

indicators.note: the clue openly says the letters of loves are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Puzzle lovers know a rearrangement is there to be cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a problem is to work out its answer.

clue.text: The second man to hoist a flag?

definitions.text: The second man to hoist a flag?

parts.words: The second man to hoist a flag?
parts.note: to raise a flag is to run it up, so someone who does that would be a runner of the flag up the pole; also the person who comes second

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a second explorer reaching a summit; the answer is the competitor who finishes second, punning on running up a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner-up is the competitor who finishes second in a race or contest.

clue.text: The Spanish red rose wine ingredients come from it

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: rose, in a down clue, says the word for red climbs upwards so it reads in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish red rosé is made from these components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red rose' looks like a flower or a rosé wine, but 'rose' turns RED upward to DER, under EL.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder tree gives elderflowers and elderberries, both used in making home-made wines.

clue.text: Part of a movement set to swing time

definitions.text: Part of a movement set to swing time

parts.words: Part of a movement set to swing time
parts.note: a clock's movement is its mechanism, and one part swings to and fro to keep the time

explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' and 'swing time' suggest music or politics; the movement is a clock's mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum is the swinging weight in a clock mechanism that regulates its timekeeping.

clue.text: Drug user did wrong, breaking law

indicators.note: breaking says the rearranged letters split open the word for law

parts.note: an act of Parliament is a law

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of did are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone taking narcotics committed a crime and broke the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads naturally as a criminal record; 'wrong' and 'breaking' are both indicators, one rearranging and one inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is someone dependent on a drug, a habitual drug user.

clue.text: Meat in an iron container cooked in blazing brandy

indicators.note: in tells us the word for meat goes inside the symbol for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: Meat is placed in a cast-iron pot and set alight with brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron container' suggests a pan, but 'iron' gives FE and 'container' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish served flambé has had brandy poured over it and set alight.

clue.text: Avoidance of supposedly unhealthy habits

parts.note: habits here means clothes, so this is the practice of shunning clothing on health grounds

explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' looks like behaviour such as smoking, but a habit is also a garment, as a monk wears.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturism is the practice of going without clothes, often promoted as healthy.
